description.value: This study compared abstinent alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls on BOLD responses during successful response inhibition and successful reactions to go stimuli in an alcohol-related go/no-go task.

spans.text: Nineteen abstinent alcohol-dependent patients (ADP) and 21 healthy control subjects (HC) were compared on blood oxygen level-dependent (BOLD) responses during successful inhibition of no-go stimuli and successful reactions to go stimuli.

value: we expected that ADP would commit more inhibitory errors in the alcohol-specific go/no-go task (AGN task) than HC and that ADP would show a significantly different neuronal activation pattern during inhibition in areas associated with response inhibition, such as the dlPFC, ACC and IFG.

spans.text: In line with previous findings, we expected that ADP would commit more inhibitory errors in the alcohol-specific go/no-go task (AGN task) than HC and that ADP would show a significantly different neuronal activation pattern during inhibition in areas associated with response inhibition, such as the dlPFC, ACC and IFG.

description.value: The study included abstinent alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls in a between-group fMRI study using an alcohol go/no-go task.

spans.text: Nineteen abstinent alcohol-dependent patients (ADP) and 21 healthy control subjects (HC) were compared on blood oxygen level-dependent (BOLD) responses during successful inhibition of no-go stimuli and successful reactions to go stimuli.

name.value: Alcohol nogo > Non-alcohol go: ADP > HC

definition.value: Comparing correctly rejected no-go trials with alcoholic stimuli to correctly responded go trials with non-alcoholic stimuli, ADP showed significantly stronger BOLD activity relative to HC.

spans.text: ADP showed significantly stronger BOLD activity

value: ADP showed significantly stronger BOLD activity than HC during correctly rejected no-go trials with alcoholic stimuli compared with correctly responded go trials with non-alcoholic stimuli, in a right-hemispheric occipital cluster composed of the lingual gyrus, right superior occipital gyrus and right middle occipital gyrus.

spans.text: ADP showed significantly stronger BOLD activity in a right-hemispheric cluster in the occipital lobe composed of the lingual gyrus, right superior occipital gyrus and the right middle occipital gyrus

name.value: Geometric nogo > geometric go: HC > ADP

definition.value: Comparing correctly rejected neutral (geometrical) no-go stimuli with correctly responded neutral go stimuli, HC showed significantly stronger BOLD activity relative to ADP.

spans.text: HC only showed increased activity relative to ADP

value: HC showed increased activity relative to ADP during correctly rejected neutral geometrical no-go stimuli compared with correctly responded neutral go stimuli, in a cluster consisting of the left postcentral gyrus and left inferior parietal lobule.

spans.text: significantly stronger BOLD activation in ADP relative to HC

value: The interaction contrast revealed significantly stronger BOLD activation in ADP relative to HC in three clusters located in occipital brain areas: right superior and middle occipital gyri and right cuneus; left middle and superior occipital gyri; and right lingual gyrus, right cerebellum and right fusiform gyrus.

spans.text: The interaction contrast (3) revealed significantly stronger BOLD activation in ADP relative to HC in three clusters located in occipital brain areas

definition.value: Main effect: [(Alcohol_nogo and Geometric_nogo) > (Nonalcohol_go and Geometric_go)], ADP > HC.

value: For the main effect comparing all correctly rejected no-go trials with correctly responded go trials, ADP showed significantly increased BOLD activity relative to HC in a left-hemispheric cluster composed of the anterior cingulate gyrus, medial frontal gyrus and medial orbitofrontal cortex.

spans.text: The comparison of all successful inhibition trials versus all go trials (main effect) revealed significantly higher BOLD activity in ADP compared to HC, but in a left hemispheric cluster comprised of the anterior cingulate gyrus, medial frontal gyrus and medial orbitofrontal cortex.

description.value: A rapid event-related alcohol go/no-go task displaying alcoholic beverages, non-alcoholic beverages and geometrical figures.

spans.text: To assess impairment of response inhibition, an alcohol go/no-go task (AGN) that displayed visual stimuli of alcoholic beverages, non-alcoholic beverages or geometrical figures was used.
The AGN task was presented with a rapid event-related design format while subjects were lying in the scanner and their brain activity was monitored with BOLD fMRI.

description.value: Functional images were preprocessed with slice-time correction, realignment, coregistration, anatomical segmentation, normalization to MNI space using DARTEL, and 8-mm Gaussian smoothing.

spans.text: The first five scans were discarded to avoid artefacts due to magnetic saturation effects and the remaining 305 images were preprocessed with the following steps: (1) slice time correction with the middle slice as reference slice, (2) realignment of scans to the first image to correct for head motion, (3) coregistration to the mean functional image and segmentation of the anatomical image using the new segment algorithm, (4) normalization of functional images to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space using SPM’s DARTEL toolbox, (5) smoothing with an 8-mm Gaussian kernel (full width at half maximum).

spans.text: The preprocessed images were analysed statistically with a general linear model (GLM) approach, by convolving the correct responses to each type of stimulus with the canonical hemodynamic response function.

model_settings.value: SPM8 GLM; correct-trial regressors convolved with the canonical HRF; incorrect responses included as regressors; six movement parameters and global mean as nuisance regressors; high-pass filter cutoff 128 s; temporal autocorrelation modeled with AR(1); group comparisons performed with two-sample t-tests; cluster-level FWE correction p < 0.05 with voxelwise cluster-defining threshold p < 0.005 uncorrected.

spans.text: The data were high pass filtered (cutoff = 128 s) and corrected for temporal auto correlations using the AR (1) model.

For the t tests, we used a family-wise error (FWE)-corrected cluster-level significance (Nichols and Hayasaka 2003 ) of p < 0.05 (at a cluster defining single-voxel significance level of p < 0.005 uncorrected).
